sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Gaurav Srivastav,Rajesh Kumar Srivastava
Hon'ble Vivek Varma,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed by counsel for the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Kamlesh Kumar Dwivedi, counsel for the applicant, Sri Rajesh Kumar Srivastava,
counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A. for the State-opposite party.
3.

The instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 123 of 2021 under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120B I.P.C., Police Station- Shahganj, District- Agra, during the pendency of the trial.
4. Counsel for the applicant contends that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.

Placing reliance upon the conclusion drawn by the Investigating Officer vide Parcha dated Vikas Chaurasia vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159267405/
1 28.03.2021 annexed as Annexure- SA-1 to the supplementary affidavit, it is submitted that the informant is also involved in the alleged transaction.

entities.text: Parcha dated Vikas Chaurasia vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, there is no clarity at the moment with regard to the role of the applicant.
It is next contended that after the said conclusion drawn by the Investigating Officer, the case was transferred to the Crime Branch, Agra.
Thereafter, the statement of the victims were again recorded by the Investigating Officer.
In the said statements, the victims again reiterated that the money was handed-over to the informant.
It is further submitted that in order to save himself, the informant has lodged the instant prosecution.

Further, the co-accused,
Manoj Kumar Mohanty, has been granted interim bail by this Court in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No. 6458 of 2023 vide order dated 15.06.2023.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No. 6458 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The applicant is in jail since 09.07.2023, having no criminal history.
In case he is enlarged on bail, he will not misuse the said liberty.
5. Learned A.G.A. and counsel for the applicant have opposed the prayer for bail but could not satisfactorily dispute the aforesaid submissions from the record.
6. Having heard counsel for the parties and having perused the record this Court prima facie finds that at present there is no clarity with regard to the role of the applicant.
As per the Parcha dated 28.03.2021 and the statement of the victims, the amount as alleged in the F.I.R. was handed over to the informant.
The inconsistencies in the F.I.R. and the statement of the victims discredit the prosecution case.

Further, the applicant has no criminal antecedent and has remained confined for more than two months and after submission of the charge-sheet there is no hope of early conclusion of trial, more so when no reasonable apprehension has been brought to the fore by the State that the applicant, if enlarged on bail, would either tamper with the evidence or delay the trial or intimidate the witness, without commenting on merits of the case
, I am of the opinion that the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.

Order Date :- 19.9.2023 Sachin Mishra  Vikas Chaurasia vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159267405/
